newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to easier.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to easier on Tuesday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate slipped slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were steady to slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.85/2.80 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.93/2.88 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.72/2.67 percent against Monday's 2.75/2.70 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$98.53/98.58.
May 2002 ended at S$99.33/99.38 versus Monday's close of S$99.38/99.43 and June 2003 at S$94.35/94.40 against S$94.39/94.44.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent from Monday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
